examples.vi: Kỳ thi khó đến mức không thể tin được đối với hầu hết học sinh.

senses.vi: cực kỳ; vô cùng; không thể tin được

senses.definition: used to say that something happened although it seemed very unlikely or surprising

examples.en: Unbelievably, nobody was hurt in the serious car crash.
examples.vi: Thật khó tin là không ai bị thương trong vụ tai nạn xe hơi nghiêm trọng đó.

senses.vi: thật khó tin; đáng kinh ngạc là

senses.definition: in a way that seems impossible or very hard to believe as true

examples.en: He told his story so unbelievably that the police doubted him.
examples.vi: Anh ta kể lại câu chuyện một cách khó tin đến mức cảnh sát phải nghi ngờ anh ta.

senses.vi: một cách khó tin

thesaurus.definition: not easy to believe

examples: He gestured unbelievably. Everyone knew he was faking his illness.
wiktionary.gloss: In a manner that one does not or cannot believe.

examples: His face turned unbelievably blue. We realized he was actually choking.
wiktionary.gloss: To an extent not to be believed.

examples: Unbelievably, Rudy saved the man's life but got sued for breaking two of his ribs.
wiktionary.gloss: Contrary to expectations, amazingly.

blocks.etymology: From un- + dreamt.

thesaurus.definition: not imagined even in a dream

examples: In the end, he regretted only the words left unspoken and the dreams left undreamt.
wiktionary.gloss: Not dreamed; not dreamt.

blocks.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *sek-? Proto-Indo-European *-(i)yós

senses.definition: Not based on scientific principles, methods, or facts.

examples.en: Her claims were rejected because they relied on unscientific testing.
examples.vi: Những tuyên bố của cô ấy bị bác bỏ vì dựa trên cách kiểm nghiệm phi khoa học.

examples.en: It is unscientific to draw conclusions from just one example.
examples.vi: Thật không khoa học khi đưa ra kết luận chỉ từ một ví dụ duy nhất.

senses.vi: không khoa học; phi khoa học

vi_block: Không khoa học; phi khoa học.

wiktionary.gloss: Not scientific

blocks.etymology: A borrowing of Italian violoncello (“little violone”), from violone (“an early form of the double bass”) + -cello (“-elle”, forming diminutives), violone itself being derived from viola + -one (“-oon”, forming augmentatives).

thesaurus.definition: a large stringed instrument; seated player holds it upright while playing

wiktionary.gloss: Synonym of cello.

thesaurus.definition: a group of people working together temporarily until some goal is achieved

wiktionary.gloss: An interdisciplinary collaboration of researchers working on new research activities that would be difficult to develop under traditional funding mechanisms such as federal agencies.
Any more or less formal team working for a specific purpose.
wiktionary.vi: nhóm làm việc; nhóm công tác

thesaurus.definition: memory for intermediate results that must be held during thinking

wiktionary.gloss: A cognitive system with a limited capacity that can hold information temporarily.
